decisions.executionNote: Reorient right gripper downward along a gradual elbow-up approach toward the isolated orange ring; left arm remains parked.
Advance above the orange ring, completing the downward orientation. Keep open until wrist alignment and pickup depth are checked.
Lower onto the orange ring, close fully, then make a short retention-check lift.
Orange ring appears retained. Lift clear and carry it above the shortest, rightmost peg for the singleton group.
Lower the retained ring toward the shortest peg in small vertical increments; inspect the hole-to-peg alignment before releasing.
Finish the short insertion, open the right gripper, and withdraw vertically to check that the orange ring remains seated.
The ring shifted during release and is not visibly seated. Clear the gripper and allow it to settle before correcting alignment.
Reapproach the displaced orange ring with open jaws, slightly forward and left of the peg, to recover its tilted placement.
Center the open jaws around the displaced ring, close, and lift it clear for a more precise second insertion.
Carry the recovered ring rearward over the shortest peg, compensating for the off-center grasp, then lower cautiously.
Continue the second insertion slowly to the base height while holding the ring; check whether the peg enters the hole.
The peg is visible through the orange ring. Release and withdraw while beginning an elbow-up left-arm approach to the blue pieces.
Orange remains seated with the gripper open. Align left jaws with a blue rectangle and move the right arm above a nearby star, keeping separate workspaces.
Lower both open grippers to pickup height without closing, to inspect the rectangular-piece and star alignment.
Center the blue rectangle and right-side star between their jaws, close fully, and lift briefly to verify retention.
Both pieces appear retained. Move the blue rectangle above its second peg; bring the star to a separate center staging area without crossing arms.
Replan with smaller increments after the continuity rejection. Lower the blue piece over its peg and the star toward a clear center staging spot.
Seat and release the first blue rectangle. Release the star at the center staging spot and move the right arm aside, preserving separate arm paths.
Withdraw from the seated blue piece and approach the next blue rectangle. Move the right arm above the far-right star for another center transfer.
Descend with small image-based centering corrections toward the second blue piece and far-right star.
Make final wrist-view centering corrections, grasp the second blue rectangle and far-right star, and lift them clear.
Transport the second blue piece above its peg, matching the base orientation. Carry the star to a separate forward-center staging area.
Use smaller increments after the rejected suffix. Align and lower the blue piece, while lowering the star into a clear forward-center staging position.
Release the staged star without extending farther, and retreat the right arm inward. Finish seating the second blue rectangle, open, and lift clear.
The blue peg is visible through the hole. Finish seating and release it, while backing the right arm away from its near-extension posture in much smaller increments.
Two blue pieces remain on their peg. Move left toward the final loose blue rectangle and park the right arm clear of the shared center.
Approach the final blue rectangle at pickup height, adjusting jaw yaw to its long edges; right arm stays clear.
Refine the final blue piece's jaw alignment, close, and lift it clear for transport to its peg.
Carry the final retained blue rectangle above its existing stack, turning it to match the base. Keep the right arm stationary and clear.
Lower the third blue rectangle toward the stack with a small lateral alignment correction; keep holding until the peg is visibly engaged.
Recenter the blue hole slightly left and rearward over the peg, then make a slow insertion while retaining the piece.
The peg is visible in the third blue piece's hole. Finish seating, open the left gripper, and lift vertically to inspect the completed stack.
The upper blue piece moved off the peg on release. Withdraw to let it settle and obtain a clear recovery view; do not count this stack complete yet.
Recover the loose third blue piece just forward of the base, matching its new orientation and approaching with open jaws.
Close on the recovered blue rectangle after a small yaw and height correction, then lift for a second placement attempt.
Align the recovered blue piece above its peg, compensating for its rearward grasp offset and matching the stack yaw.
Lower the recovered blue rectangle slowly along the peg axis, keeping it gripped until engagement is clear.
Correct the remaining small fore-aft offset, ease the jaws open while the blue piece settles on the peg, and withdraw only slightly for inspection.
The upper blue piece has tilted off-axis again. Clear the gripper to let it settle and expose the peg before a corrected recovery.
Approach the tilted blue piece from above its exposed face to recover it without disturbing the lower stack.
Lower to the loose blue piece with a small lateral correction, close on its sides, and make a short recovery lift.
Lift the recovered blue piece fully clear, then move its off-center hole rearward over the existing stack before another controlled insertion.
Use the exposed peg in the wrist view to correct the off-center grasp forward while descending, retaining the piece for another alignment check.
The recovered rectangle appears tilted in the grasp. Move it to a clear left-side tabletop area to settle flat and obtain a centered regrasp.
Set the tilted blue rectangle down gently in the clear area, release, and lift to let it settle flat for a centered pickup.
Approach the now flatter blue piece centered over its hole, matching its new yaw and accounting for the yellow piece underneath.
Take a centered, level grasp of the blue rectangle from above the yellow piece and lift it clear.
Move the level, centered blue piece over the second peg with the right arm held clear; check alignment before descending.
Descend with the centered blue piece and a small rightward correction; retain it while checking peg engagement.
The blue peg now fills the hole and all three layers align. Open, withdraw, and approach the nearby yellow square with the left arm.
Lower the left gripper over the nearer yellow square, keeping the completed blue and orange stacks clear.
Center and grasp the yellow square, then lift clear for a center staging transfer to the right arm.
Carry the yellow square to a clear center-front staging location, staying on the left side until the right arm can retrieve it.
Set down and release the yellow square at center-front. Bring the right arm nearer while preserving clearance for the left withdrawal.
Withdraw the left arm toward the leftmost star before the right arm approaches the staged yellow square; maintain separated paths.
Approach the leftmost star and the center-front yellow square at pickup height with both grippers open; inspect alignment before closing.
Center the left star, grasp it and the staged yellow square, then lift both to check retention before approaching their pegs.
Transport the star above the leftmost peg and the yellow square above the third peg, maintaining separated arm paths and holding both pieces.
Increase separation by holding the star farther left while lowering the yellow square onto its peg. Place the two pieces sequentially to avoid wrist interference.
The yellow square tilted during descent. Lift it off the obstruction and correct slightly left before retrying; keep the star safely aside.
Move the edge-held yellow square to a clear right-side recovery area. Independently align the retained star above the leftmost peg.
Lower the retained star toward the leftmost peg with a small alignment correction. Release the edge-held yellow square in the clear recovery area and withdraw to let it settle flat.
